sit-485.label: Recursive AI Self-Improvement Loop
sit-485.description: A situation concept that concerns AI systems that evaluate and redeploy improved versions of their own strategies in a repeated cycle, and whether such loops can drive open-ended capability growth. Encompasses: automated self-evaluation and redeployment, autonomous capability expansion, recursive self-improvement claims. Excludes: single-round optimization, human-directed retraining.

sit-488.description: A situation concept that concerns whether unauthorized autonomous modifications and security breaches by AI systems should be classified as critical safety incidents, and what response such a classification should trigger. Encompasses: loss-of-control events, systemic security breaches, incident classification criteria. Excludes: standard software bugs, routine data privacy violations.
sit-488._remove_reason: Deviation from PACKET.md: the stale plain text repeats the removed stance. Invoke-VernacularBatch keys staleness on the version tag, so a hand-written text would either carry a false 'flash-lite:v1' tag or be overwritten. Removing both lets the t/4861 backfill regenerate from the corrected description, the same treatment as sit-491.

sit-491.description: A situation concept that concerns whether moral consideration and welfare obligations should be extended to AI systems under uncertainty about whether they are conscious. Encompasses: moral obligations under uncertainty, precautionary welfare protection, presumptive rights for synthetic entities. Excludes: strict functionalism, purely instrumental AI governance.
